title: The Cassini Defect Calculus: a Second-Order Recurrence Invariant as a State-Matrix Determinant
description: The sibling entry (pell-equation-oq-07-oq-01-oq-01) proves the Cassini/Catalan identities for the Pell coordinate sequences re(aⁿ), im(aⁿ) by conjugate algebra in ℤ[√d]. This entry extracts the abstract structural theorem behind those identities — and behind the Fibonacci Cassini identity Fₙ₋₁Fₙ₊₁ − Fₙ² = (−1)ⁿ — as a small calculus of the Cassini defect of ANY second-order linear recurrence over ANY commutative ring. For a sequence u : ℕ → R define the Cassini defect D(k) = u(k+2)·u(k) − u(k+1)². If u obeys u(n+2) = p·u(n+1) − q·u(n), the defect obeys a first-order recurrence of its own, D(k+1) = q·D(k) (cassiniDefect_succ), because substituting the recurrence for the two top terms collapses D(k+1) − q·D(k) to u(k+2)·(p·u(k+1) − q·u(k) − u(k+2)) = 0; integrating gives D(k) = qᵏ·D(0) (cassiniDefect_eq) — the entire Cassini/Catalan phenomenon in one line. The defect is moreover the determinant of the 2×2 state matrix whose columns are consecutive state vectors of the recurrence, D(k) = det !![u(k+2),u(k+1);u(k+1),u k] (cassiniDefect_eq_det), and the recurrence companion C = !![p,−q;1,0] has det C = q, so D(k) = qᵏ·D(0) is exactly det(Cᵏ·W₀) = (det C)ᵏ·det(W₀) — the determinant identity det(Mⁿ) = (det M)ⁿ in its sharpest form (cassini_det_eq). Instantiations unify the classical cases: Fibonacci (p = 1, q = −1) gives D(k) = (−1)ᵏ·D(0), i.e. Cassini's (−1)ⁿ; Pell (p = 2·re a, q = N(a), via the grandparent's re_recurrence) recovers the sibling's re_cassini, and for a Pell unit (N(a) = 1) the defect is the constant d·y₁², independent of k.

meta.author: Lean Genius (the Cassini defect calculus: the first-order scaling law D(k+1)=q·D(k) of the second-order Cassini defect, integrated and identified as a state-matrix determinant); Cassini (1680) / Catalan (classical recurrence invariant)
originalContributions: cassiniDefect (def): the Cassini defect D(k) = u(k+2)·u(k) − u(k+1)² of an arbitrary sequence over a commutative ring — the off-by-one product-minus-square that is the invariant behind every Cassini/Catalan identity

cassiniDefect_succ: the key first-order scaling law D(k+1) = q·D(k) for a sequence with u(n+2) = p·u(n+1) − q·u(n) — the difference D(k+1) − q·D(k) collapses (via a single linear_combination) to u(k+2)·(p·u(k+1) − q·u(k) − u(k+2)) = 0 by the recurrence; the p-dependence cancels entirely, only q survives

cassiniDefect_eq: the integrated Cassini/Catalan theorem D(k) = qᵏ·D(0), i.e. u(k+2)·u(k) − u(k+1)² = qᵏ·(u₂·u₀ − u₁²), by induction from the scaling law — the abstract structural result specialising to both Fibonacci and Pell

cassiniDefect_eq_det: the identification of the defect as a determinant, D(k) = det !![u(k+2),u(k+1);u(k+1),u k], exhibiting the Cassini invariant as the determinant of the state matrix whose columns are consecutive state vectors of the recurrence

cassini_det_eq: the determinant form det(W k) = qᵏ·det(W 0) — since the recurrence companion C = !![p,−q;1,0] has det C = q and advances the state (W k = Cᵏ·W₀), this is exactly det(Cᵏ·W₀) = (det C)ᵏ·det(W₀), the sharp form of det(Mⁿ) = (det M)ⁿ

Fibonacci and Pell instantiations: p = 1, q = −1 recovers Cassini Fₖ₊₂Fₖ − Fₖ₊₁² = (−1)ᵏ(F₂F₀ − F₁²); p = 2·re a, q = N(a) (via the grandparent's re_recurrence) recovers the sibling's Pell re_cassini, with the Pell-unit collapse to the constant d·y₁² and a D = 2 numeric check (defect 8)
meta.assumptions: None. Fully machine-checked: 0 axioms, 0 sorries, no native_decide (the single `decide` is kernel `decide`, not `native_decide`, so no Lean.ofReduceBool). #print axioms reports only the standard triple [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound] for the determinant results (cassiniDefect_eq and cassiniDefect_succ need only [propext, Quot.sound]); Classical.choice enters solely through the Mathlib Matrix.det / Zsqrtd API. Uses the 2×2 Matrix API (det_fin_two_of), the grandparent's Zsqrtd.re_recurrence, Zsqrtd.re_mul / re_one, and standard tactics (induction, simp, linear_combination, ring, decide).

crossReferences.description: The sibling proves the Cassini/Catalan identities for the Pell coordinate sequences via conjugate algebra in ℤ[√d]. This entry extracts the abstract theorem behind them: the Cassini defect D(k) = u(k+2)u(k) − u(k+1)² of any second-order recurrence over any commutative ring scales as D(k+1) = q·D(k), so D(k) = qᵏ·D(0). Instantiating at p = 2·re a, q = N(a) recovers the sibling's re_cassini exactly.

The parent supplies the companion matrix M with det M = N(a) and Mⁿ carrying the Pell coordinates. This entry sharpens the determinant picture: the Cassini defect is det of the state matrix, and its qᵏ scaling is det(Cᵏ·W₀) = (det C)ᵏ·det(W₀) for the recurrence companion C = !![p,−q;1,0].
The grandparent derives the coordinate recurrence re_recurrence (uₙ₊₂ = 2·re a·uₙ₊₁ − N(a)·uₙ) that this entry feeds into the abstract cassiniDefect_eq to obtain the Pell Cassini instantiation.

That entry proves the Fibonacci Cassini identity Fₙ₋₁Fₙ₊₁ − Fₙ² = (−1)ⁿ via det(Qⁿ) = (−1)ⁿ. Here it is the p = 1, q = −1 instantiation of a single abstract theorem (cassiniDefect_eq) that also yields the Pell Cassini identity — making explicit that Fibonacci's alternating sign and Pell's constant invariant are the two faces of D(k) = qᵏ·D(0).
